papers.title: Factors associated with communicative and financial barriers to healthcare utilization among people with selected citizenships in Germany: results from a nationwide cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Research has shown that migrants in Germany face various barriers to healthcare access, including communicative and financial barriers. This study examined which sociodemographic, migration-related, and psychosocial factors are associated with these barriers in order to better understand lower healthcare utilization among migrants. METHODS: We used data from the nationwide cross-sectional health interview survey GEDA Fokus, which included people with Croatian, Italian, Polish, Syrian, or Turkish citizenship living in Germany. Descriptive, univariable, and multivariable analyses were conducted separately for communicative and financial barriers while accounting for relevant social factors. RESULTS: Of the 6,038 participants, 16.2% reported communicative barriers and 9.0% reported financial barriers to healthcare utilization. According to the regression analyses, gender, age, German language proficiency, and self-reported experiences of racist discrimination were associated with communicative barriers. For financial barriers, associations with gender, educational level, and experiences of discrimination due to the socioeconomic situation were found. CONCLUSION: The results indicate that demographic, socioeconomic, migration-related, and psychosocial factors are associated with communicative and financial barriers to healthcare utilization. Gender and experiences of discrimination were significantly associated with both communicative and financial barriers. In practice, the provision of qualified translation and interpretation services, anti-discrimination and awareness training for healthcare staff, and the expansion of low-threshold, financially accessible services could help promote more equitable access to healthcare among migrants.

papers.title: Advancing a Model of Mindful Sexual Communication: Testing Sexual Communication as a Mediator of the Association Between Sexual Mindfulness and Sexual Satisfaction.
papers.abstract: Mindfulness and communication have powerful implications for sexual health. Sexual communication and sexual mindfulness - the ability to be aware and non-judgmental during sexual activity - are two constructs often associated with sexual satisfaction. To further explore these relationships, a model of mindful sexual communication was advanced. More specifically, a moderated mediation model was tested to explore the indirect effect of sexual mindfulness on sexual satisfaction through sexual communication, as well as the potential moderating role of interoceptive awareness (i.e., trusting the body and self-regulation). Data were collected from 205 young adult college students in a variety of relational contexts that had a recent sexual interaction. The results indicated that sexual mindfulness awareness was indirectly associated with sexual satisfaction via frequency and comfort of sexual communication, whereas sexual mindfulness non-judgment was only indirectly associated with sexual satisfaction via sexual communication comfort. Additionally, two moderated mediation models were supported for participants in committed relationships: trusting the body and self-regulation moderated the indirect effect of sexual mindfulness non-judgment on sexual satisfaction via sexual communication comfort. The results reveal that different aspects of sexual mindfulness function uniquely together with aspects of sexual communication and interoceptive awareness to predict sexual satisfaction, revealing preliminary support for a new theoretical model of mindful sexual communication. These findings and their implications for sexual communication and mindfulness are discussed along with practical applications for individuals and professionals.

papers.title: The role of sexual mindfulness in enhancing sexual well-being among breast cancer survivors: A randomized clinical trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with a wide range of sexual disorders are vulnerable to negative sexual well-being due to complications from breast cancer treatment. This study aimed to investigate the impact of sexual mindfulness-based training on the sexual well-being of women with breast cancer. METHODS: This randomized clinical trial was conducted in 2024 and involved a statistical population of women with breast cancer who had consulted comprehensive health service centers in Shahrekord, Iran. Among the referring women, 36 people were selected by convenience sampling. To investigate depression in the participants, the short-form Beck Depression Questionnaire was used, and 4 patients were excluded from the study due to severe depression. Then, the participants were randomly assigned to 2 study groups of 16 patients.Sexual mindfulness training was conducted in 8 sessions (90 minutes, once a week) for the intervention group at the reproductive and sexual health clinic in Shahrekord. Meanwhile, the control group was not subjected to planned intervention or training. A sexual well-being questionnaire was used to collect data for repeated measures analysis. Both groups were asked to complete the sexual well-being questionnaire before, immediately after, and 3 months after the intervention. Data were analyzed through independent samples T-test, analysis of covariance, and repeated measures analysis. RESULTS: The findings showed that there was no significant difference in sexual well-being between the intervention and control groups before the intervention (P = .29). Immediately after the intervention, sexual well-being significantly increased in the intervention group, from 39.33 ± 25.56 to 56.17 ± 22.29 (P < .001); however, the corresponding between-group comparison was not statistically significant (P = .11). Three months after the intervention, sexual well-being was significantly higher in the intervention group (66.42 ± 13.79) than in the control group (51.92 ± 20.62; P < .001). CONCLUSION: Sexual Mindfulness can be considered a therapeutic method in palliative care to improve sexual well-being in breast cancer patients.

papers.title: A Multilayer Visibility Graph Framework for Ultrashort-Term Analysis of Multichannel Physiological Signals.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in physiological sensing technologies enable continuous acquisition of multichannel biosignals for digital health applications. Because physiological interactions arise from nonlinear mechanisms, their characterization requires analytical approaches capable of capturing both individual signal dynamics and cross-signal dependencies, often from short recordings. This study proposes a multilayer visibility graph (VG) framework free of phase-space embedding parameters for analyzing physiological interactions from multichannel biosignals. The approach was evaluated in a simulation study based on unidirectionally coupled Rössler oscillators and in two physiological datasets comprising synchronized cardiovascular recordings from healthy adults and wearable electrodermal activity (EDA) recordings acquired during a Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) intervention. Average Degree (DA) was used to characterize the topological organization of individual and multiplex visibility graphs, while inter-layer mutual information (I) between degree sequences was introduced to quantify cross-layer dependence. In the simulation study, coupling-related changes in the response dynamics were already detectable from single-layer VGs at short window lengths, whereas inter-layer mutual information captured coupling-dependent changes in cross-layer organization. Feature estimates began to stabilize at approximately 480 samples and approached a plateau at longer window lengths. In the cardiovascular dataset, sex-related differences were primarily observed in configurations involving systolic blood pressure: DA differed in single-layer and multichannel representations, while inter-layer mutual information showed significant sex differences, specifically in the interbeat interval-systolic blood pressure duplex. In the EDA dataset, the proposed descriptors identified changes in trainer-trainee physiological organization across the MBSR intervention. These findings indicate that VG-based descriptors provide complementary information on within-signal topology and inter-layer dependence and can be applied to short multichannel physiological recordings without phase-space reconstruction.
